scope: GTK2 normal vertical scrollbar thumb start: compare the user screenshot to Motif, isolate the two-row transition, generate an orientation-specific role-driven asset, and apply it through the GTK2 palette pipeline.

finding.geometry: GTK2 and Motif bar width are both 15 px. Normal upper arrow remains a 15x15 cell; its normalized shape/relevo match.

before_transition.classification: At thumb start: GTK2 added a full-width light cap for two rows, while SR10.4 starts with the normal cross-axis thumb profile.

finding.cause: The generic 24x24 GTK2 thumb pixmap contributed a two-row horizontal top cap when rendered at the vertical scrollbar start. It overlaid the continuous cross-axis relief measured in the canonical Motif reference.
finding.palette: Only generated pixels derived from the existing KDE face/light/shadow roles were reused. No final RGB was introduced.

candidate.implementation: Generate scroll-thumb-normal-vertical.png from the palette-rendered normal thumb, copying its first body row into its two top 9-slice rows; route only the NORMAL VERTICAL slider to it. Horizontal and other states are unchanged.
candidate.preview: GTK2 2.24.33 native fixture, private Xvfb :223, GtkAdjustment value 0, page size 250, vertical allocation 15x255; explicit generated palette RC.

changes: tools/gtk2_domainos_palette.py generates and routes the normal vertical thumb continuation asset.
GTK2 semantic palette refreshed for lsi through the existing journaled pipeline; 179 native reload events sent.
limits: Only the normal vertical thumb start is compared and changed.
Horizontal thumb caps, pressed/disabled states and direct VUE interaction remain open.
Native isolated rendering proves the asset/preview; human visual acceptance in the open XChat remains pending.
result: The first two thumb transition rows now match the canonical SR10.4 Motif profile exactly in the native GTK2 preview. The application change was applied without restarting XChat; human visual review remains open.

coverage_estimate.basis: Existing GTK2 technical coverage estimate; no percentage claim about visual fidelity.
